summary.one_line: Not an equity IPO: SMCG04 is SMC Global's fourth public issue of secured, ICRA A (Stable) rated NCDs (₹75 cr base + ₹75 cr green shoe, ₹1,000 face value). It is a loan to a 30-year-old, mid-sized, promoter-run broking/insurance-broking/NBFC group whose credit is adequate but has been weakening: FY26 profit fell to ₹103 cr, gearing is rising and capital-market regulation has tightened. The final 2026 coupon and objects could not be verified from the prospectus itself.
bull_points: Secured paper: principal and interest are backed by a pari passu charge on trade receivables and the margin-trading-facility (MTF) book, with a stated 110% asset cover (S1, S2).

ICRA reaffirmed [ICRA]A (Stable) on 7 Aug 2026, citing a 30-year track record, a diversified mix (broking, MTF, insurance broking, distribution, NBFC) and adequate capitalisation: consolidated net worth ₹1,341 cr and gearing 1.5x at 30 Jun 2026 (S6).
Consolidated revenue grew every year, from ₹1,212 cr in FY23 to ₹1,776 cr in FY25 and about ₹1,878 cr in FY26 (S4, S7). Q1 FY27 PAT recovered 22% YoY to ₹36.7 cr on ₹515 cr of revenue (S8).

The issuer has run three earlier retail NCD issues of the same size and structure since July 2024 (S10, S11, S12). The October 2025 issue was 2.13x subscribed (S13), and 24-month NCDs from the 2024 issue have been redeemed at maturity (S21).
bear_points: Profitability is falling. Consolidated PAT went ₹188 cr (FY24) → ₹147 cr (FY25) → ₹103 cr (FY26), and RoNW fell to 8.2% against a five-year average of 14.6% (S4, S6).

FY26 PBT/net operating income was 21.4%, and 20.6% in capital-market businesses. ICRA's negative rating trigger is below 20% in that segment on a sustained basis, so there is very little headroom (S6).

The business depends on regulation and is shrinking in share. Its retail cash-market share fell from 1.8% (FY22) to 0.7% (FY26), NSE active clients are about 1.6 lakh (0.35%), about 40% of gross broking income comes from derivatives, and the April 2026 F&O STT hike and the July 2026 RBI curbs on bank funding for proprietary trading both hit it directly (S6, S14, S15).

Leverage and liquidity are tighter. Standalone gearing rose from 0.9x (Mar-25) to 1.3x (Jun-26). Of ₹1,352 cr standalone borrowings, ₹624 cr falls due within six months, against only ₹152 cr of unused lines and ₹2 cr of unencumbered cash (S6). Standalone operating cash flow was negative in FY23, FY24 and FY25 (S4).

The litigation load is heavy and growing: 16 criminal and 6 statutory/regulatory proceedings against the company, 70 disciplinary actions listed, 12 criminal proceedings against promoters (mostly cheating/misappropriation complaints), and a ₹10.36 cr GST show-cause notice (S4).
watch_points: The final series-wise coupons, effective yields and objects of the October 2026 issue. Check them in the prospectus before applying. Earlier issues paid 9.75%–10.5% and allocated ≥75% to working capital (S4, S10, S11, S12).
Whether H1 FY27 profit holds the Q1 recovery once the full-year effect of the F&O STT hike and the RBI CMI lending rules shows up (S6, S8, S14, S15).
NBFC asset quality in Moneywise Financial Services. GNPA was 2.99% at Jun-26 (3.55% at Mar-25), and the book is being re-anchored to secured micro-LAP lending (S6).
Insurance broking now makes up about a third of revenue but earned only ₹1.6 cr EBIT in Q1 FY27 (S8). Watch whether it becomes profitable.
Subscription figures by category as the issue progresses. No day-1 numbers were found at the time of writing.

reasoning: This is debt, not equity, so the only question is whether SMC will repay ₹1,000 plus coupon on time. On that test the issuer clears the bar but has no margin to spare. ICRA rates it A (Stable) with adequate capitalisation (net worth ₹1,341 cr, gearing 1.5x) (S6), and the NCDs are secured on receivables and the MTF book at 110% cover (S1). But FY26 capital-market PBT/NOI of 20.6% sits right at ICRA's 20% downgrade trigger (S6).

The money raised does not build anything. If, like the October 2025 issue, at least 75% goes to working capital (exchange margins and the MTF book) and up to 25% to general corporate purposes (S4), the issue simply adds leverage to a business whose standalone gearing has already risen from 0.9x to 1.3x and whose standalone operating cash flow has been negative for three straight years (S4, S6). We could not confirm this issue's objects from the 2026 prospectus itself.

SMC has no real moat in its core business. Its retail cash-market share fell from 1.8% to 0.7% in four years, and its 1.6 lakh active NSE clients are a 0.35% share in a market where Groww, Zerodha and Angel One hold about 58% of 4.42 crore active clients (S6, S16). Its earnings are about 75% capital-market linked and therefore cyclical (S6).

The regulatory direction is against it. The F&O STT hike from 1 Apr 2026 and the RBI's July 2026 rules (full collateral, a 40% equity haircut, no bank funding for proprietary trading) hit the derivatives-heavy (~40%) broking income and the ₹138 cr of proprietary trading income directly (S6, S14, S15).

Governance needs watching but does not disqualify. The board has 7 independent directors out of 14, and the old NSEL problem at subsidiary Pulin Comtrade was settled in Sept 2026 for about ₹9.1 lakh (S4, S18). Against that, criminal complaints against promoters went from 5 to 12 between the 2024 and 2025 prospectuses, and promoters still hold 20% of the group's trademark rights (S4, S5).

Call: track rather than invest. An A-rated, secured 2–5 year paper with a long repayment record could suit a diversified fixed-income investor who caps exposure. Commit only after confirming the 2026 coupon schedule and objects in the prospectus, and after H1 FY27 results show the profit recovery is holding above ICRA's trigger levels (S6, S8).

subsections.title: What is actually being offered: a secured bond, not shares

blocks.text: Read this first. SMCG04 is not an equity IPO. SMC Global's shares have been listed on NSE and BSE since its 1995 IPO (S4). This October 2026 offer is a public issue of secured, rated, listed, redeemable non-convertible debentures (NCDs) of ₹1,000 face value. The ₹1,000 'price band' is the face value of one debenture (S1, S3). An investor is lending money to the company for a fixed term at a fixed coupon and gets no ownership stake. The rest of this report is written from that lender's point of view.

On 26 July 2026 the board approved in principle a public issue of up to 15,00,000 NCDs: a ₹7,500 lakh (₹75 cr) base issue plus an equal green-shoe option, for a total of up to ₹150 cr (S3). The NCD committee approved the draft prospectus on 16 September 2026 (S2). By 28 September 2026 the issue had BSE in-principle approval and an ICRA A (Stable) rating. It is secured by about 110% asset cover on trade receivables and MTF assets (S1). The issue opens 5 October and closes 16 October 2026, and the NCDs will list on BSE (S1, S7).

This is the fourth retail NCD issue of the same ₹75 cr + ₹75 cr structure in about two years: July 2024 (10.0%–10.4% effective yields), April 2025 (10.0%–10.5%) and October 2025 (9.75%–10.25%), each with 24-, 36- and 60-month series (S10, S11, S12). The series-wise coupons for the October 2026 issue were not visible in any source we could open. Investors must read them in the prospectus before applying.

blocks.caption: SMC Global's retail NCD issues to date (effective yields, % p.a.)

blocks.text: Sources for the table: July 2024 (S11, S5), April 2025 (S12), October 2025 (S10, S4), October 2026 (S1, S7).

SMC Global was incorporated in Delhi in December 1994 and runs a diversified financial-services group. The prospectus reports it in three segments (S4). (1) Broking, distribution and trading covers broking in equities, commodities, currency and derivatives, proprietary trading (including arbitrage and HFT), clearing, depository services, distribution of mutual funds and other third-party products, PMS, real-estate broking, mortgage advisory and investment banking. (2) Insurance broking for life and non-life policies, via SMC Insurance Brokers. (3) Financing through its NBFC, Moneywise Financial Services (MFSPL) (S4, S6).

ICRA estimates that about 75% of group net income comes from capital-market businesses (S6). Within broking, about 40% of gross broking income comes from derivatives (S6). Proprietary trading is material: ICRA counts ₹117 cr of proprietary trading income (net of STT) in FY25, ₹138 cr in FY26 and ₹51 cr in Q1 FY27, against group net operating income of ₹608 cr, ₹628 cr and ₹169 cr respectively (S6).

Segment figures from S8. The mix matters for a lender. Almost all the profit comes from broking and trading, which is the volatile, regulation-sensitive part. Insurance broking adds a third of revenue but earns almost nothing (EBIT ₹1.6 cr in Q1 FY27) (S8). The NBFC is shrinking by design (S6).

items: Customers are mainly retail and HNI investors and traders. The NBFC lends mostly to SMEs: about 68% of MFSPL AUM was SME financing at 31 Mar 2026, with unsecured SME working-capital loans down to about 25% from about 50% three to four years earlier (S6).
Q1 FY27 KPIs: broking client base of 13.8 lakh, mutual-fund AUM of ₹4,787 cr, NBFC AUM of ₹1,025 cr of which 75% is secured retail products (S9).
The 'price' is commission, brokerage, distribution fees, insurance commissions, interest on MTF and loans, and trading gains. Consolidated interest income was ₹447.6 cr in FY25 (S4).

blocks.text: SMC is a full-service, branch-and-franchisee broker rather than an app-first discount broker. At 30 June 2026 it had 198 branches and about 1,935 franchisees across 424 cities, and an active NSE client base of 1.6 lakh, a 0.35% market share (S6). A year earlier the network was 210 branches (one in Dubai) and 2,137 authorised persons in 412 cities, with 4,091 employees including outsourced staff (S4). The franchise network is shrinking. Its discount-broking arm Stoxkart (run by subsidiary Moneywise Finvest) had about 76,000 active NSE clients at June 2026, and ICRA calls its contribution 'marginal' (S6).

The model consumes a lot of capital. SMC typically places about ₹3,000 cr of margins with exchanges, and it funds those margins and its MTF book with bank and NBFC borrowings, both fund-based and non-fund-based (S6). That is why it keeps coming back to the retail debt market: these NCDs mainly refinance and extend the working-capital funding behind margins and client lending. They do not fund new capacity (S4, S6).

items: Registrations: SEBI stockbroker and depository participant (CDSL, NSDL), research analyst, portfolio manager. Member of BSE, NSE, MSEI, MCX, ICEX and NCDEX. IFSCA fund-management entity. AMFI distributor (S4).
SMC Insurance Brokers was upgraded from direct broker to composite broker (re-insurance licence) with effect from 18 Aug 2025 (S4).

SMC is also a market maker for SME IPOs. In Sept 2026 it and Moneywise together took a 26.68% stake (about ₹25.9 cr) in S.K. Offset, a BSE SME listing, because of that role (S19). This is balance-sheet risk a creditor should notice.

subsections.title: Market size and the 2026 regulatory reset

blocks.text: Indian retail broking is large but concentrated, and it is volume-driven. NSE active clients were 4.42 crore in June 2026, up 3.1% month-on-month after a weak FY26 (S16). Revenue across the industry depends on trading volumes, especially retail F&O, so regulation sets the size of the profit pool as much as demand does (S14).

Two 2026 measures hit SMC's profit pool directly. First, Budget 2026 raised STT on futures from 0.02% to 0.05% and on options premium from 0.10% to 0.15% (exercise from 0.125% to 0.15%), effective 1 April 2026, explicitly to cool retail derivatives speculation (S14). Second, the RBI's credit-facility amendment directions for capital-market intermediaries, effective after a deferral to 1 July 2026, require 100% collateral, apply a minimum 40% haircut on equity collateral and bar bank funding for brokers' own-account securities purchases (S15). ICRA names both as monitorables for SMC's broking volumes and proprietary-trading returns (S6).

blocks.caption: Regulatory changes that bear on SMC in 2026
rows: Lower derivatives volumes; ~40% of gross broking income is derivatives (S6, S14)
Same as above; also proprietary trading returns (S6, S14)

100% collateral, 40% equity haircut, no bank funding of proprietary trading

blocks.text: The market is dominated by app-based brokers. In June 2026 Groww had 1.31 crore active clients (28.7% share), Zerodha 68 lakh (15.0%) and Angel One 66 lakh (14.6%), followed by ICICI Securities (4.7%) and Upstox (4.2%). The top three hold nearly 58% of active accounts (S16). SMC, with 1.6 lakh active NSE clients (0.35%), is a small player (S6).
The top five rows are from S16 and the SMC row is from ICRA (S6). SMC is also losing share. ICRA notes its retail cash-segment market share contracted from 1.8% in FY22 to 0.7% in FY26 (S6).

No real moat in the core business. SMC has no market-share leadership, no technology or regulatory barrier that rivals lack, and no import-substitution angle. Broking is described by ICRA as 'highly competitive and fragmented' with easy entry for new players (S6). Its own active-client and cash-market share figures are falling (S6).

Its genuine advantages are softer: three decades of operating history, a physical branch and franchise network that serves offline and smaller-town investors, and a full licence stack (broking, clearing, DP, PMS, insurance broking including re-insurance, NBFC) (S4, S6). These advantages support the franchise and are the reason ICRA gives it an A rating, but they have not stopped the share loss. For a lender, a long record of surviving market cycles matters more than a moat, and SMC does have that record (S6).

The figures below for FY23–FY25 come from the audited consolidated financials reproduced in the October 2025 prospectus (S4), converted from ₹ lakh to ₹ crore. FY26 figures come from Screener and ICRA (S6, S7), because the October 2026 prospectus with restated FY26 numbers could not be opened (see method).

Revenue has grown every year, by 35% in FY24 and 8% in FY25 (S4), but profits have not. PAT peaked at ₹188 cr in FY24 and fell 22% in FY25 and another 30% in FY26 to ₹103 cr (S4, S6). ICRA attributes the FY26 fall to higher operating expenses and lower fair-value gains on investments (S6). Interest cost more than doubled from ₹89 cr (FY23) to ₹207 cr (FY25) (S4). By our calculation, (PBT + interest) / interest fell from about 2.8x in FY23 to about 1.9x in FY25. Screener also flags 'low interest coverage' (S7). Margins are compressing even as the top line grows.
Source: S6. Proprietary trading (₹138 cr) was over 20% of NOI in FY26, and FY26 PBT/NOI was 21.4% (20.6% in capital-market businesses) against a five-year average of 38.0% (S6).

subsections.title: Balance sheet, leverage and cash flow

blocks.text: Consolidated debt (debt securities plus other borrowings) rose from about ₹908 cr at FY23 to ₹1,421 cr at FY24 and ₹1,657 cr at FY25, and reached about ₹1,711 cr at June 2025 (S4). Screener shows borrowings of about ₹2,036 cr at FY26 (S7). Debt securities, which include the retail NCDs, grew from ₹40 cr at FY24 to ₹154 cr at FY25 and ₹267 cr at June 2025 (S4). Retail NCDs have become a growing part of the funding mix.

Source: S4. Operating cash flow has been negative in most periods, both consolidated and standalone, while reported profit was positive. That is partly normal for a broker, because growth in client margins, MTF loans and receivables runs through operating cash flow. But it means the business does not fund itself and depends on continuous refinancing (S4, S6). The prospectus itself lists negative cash flows as a top risk factor (S4). Screener shows a different consolidated operating cash-flow series (-₹193 cr, +₹24 cr, -₹73 cr for FY23–FY25) (S7). We use the prospectus figures and note the discrepancy.

Liquidity is the key point for a lender. At 30 June 2026 standalone borrowings were ₹1,352 cr, of which ₹624 cr was due within six months, against ₹152 cr of drawable unused lines and ₹2 cr of unencumbered cash. ICRA still rates liquidity 'adequate' because the ~₹415 cr MTF book and ~₹694 cr of receivables can be liquidated quickly (S6). Those are the same assets charged to NCD holders (S1). Standalone gearing rose from 0.9x (Mar-25) to 1.3x (Jun-26) (S6).

subsections.title: Red flags and whether the numbers support the story

items: Contingent liabilities of about ₹1,097 cr per Screener, roughly 80% of net worth (S7).
High debtor days of about 161 (S7), consistent with large client and exchange receivables (S6).
NBFC GNPA was 2.99% at Jun-26 versus 3.55% at Mar-25, with slippages from legacy exposures. NBFC return on managed assets is only 1.8% (S6).
PAT has fallen for two consecutive years (FY25, FY26) despite rising revenue (S4, S6).

blocks.text: Do the numbers support repayment? Broadly yes, with an important qualification. Net worth of ₹1,341 cr is about nine times the maximum ₹150 cr issue, and gearing of 1.5x is well inside ICRA's 2.5x trigger (S6). But the earnings trend runs against the issuer. Profitability in the capital-market segment is sitting at the threshold ICRA uses for a negative rating action (S6). The Q1 FY27 rebound (PAT ₹37 cr, RoNW about 11%) is encouraging, but ICRA itself says sustaining it 'would continue to be contingent on broader capital market activity' (S6).

A note on data mismatches. Chittorgarh labels ₹955 cr income and ₹105 cr PAT for FY25 as 'consolidated' (S13). Those are in fact the standalone figures in the prospectus. Consolidated FY25 is ₹1,786 cr income and ₹147 cr PAT (S4). This report uses the prospectus tables throughout.

blocks.text: Rating nuance: on 7 Aug 2026 ICRA assigned A (Stable) to ₹100 cr of new NCDs and reaffirmed ₹400 cr of existing NCDs, a total of ₹500 cr of rated NCDs (S6). The ₹150 cr maximum of this issue is above the ₹100 cr newly assigned figure. The headroom may come from unused amounts within the ₹400 cr already rated. That cannot be confirmed without the prospectus, and investors should check that the full issue size is covered by the rating letter.
Fresh issue vs OFS: an NCD issue is 100% fresh money borrowed by the company. There is no offer-for-sale component and no promoter selling. On the other hand, it adds leverage instead of equity.

We could not read the 'Objects of the Issue' section of the October 2026 prospectus. News coverage describes the purpose only as bolstering the capital base, financing securities operations and diversifying funding (S1). The most recent document we could read is the October 2025 prospectus for the identical ₹75 cr + ₹75 cr structure. That one allocated the net proceeds as follows (S4):

blocks.caption: Objects of the issue — October 2025 NCD issue (latest verified; the 2026 split is expected to be similar but is unconfirmed)

blocks.text: In practice, 'working capital' at a broker means funding exchange margins (about ₹3,000 cr placed at exchanges) and growing the MTF book (S6). The proceeds therefore extend and diversify SMC's funding, which is useful given the RBI's 2026 tightening of bank credit to brokers (S15). They do not create new earning capacity. The October 2025 prospectus also states that the fund requirements were not appraised by any bank or financial institution and are based on management estimates (S4).

The promoters are Subhash Chand Aggarwal (Chairman & MD; a chartered accountant with the company since 1994 and former co-chair of ASSOCHAM's capital-markets council), Mahesh C Gupta (Vice-Chairman & MD, also since 1994), Damodar Krishan Aggarwal, Sushma Gupta, and next-generation promoters Himanshu Gupta (non-executive director, heads the NBFC, fixed-income and bullion businesses) and Pranay Aggarwal (non-executive director, ex-PwC, launched Stoxkart) (S4). Promoters held 66.71% at June 2026, slightly down from 67.30% in March 2025 (S7).

blocks.text: Source: S4. The founders have run the business for more than 30 years, and the independent directors are credible, senior names. Control is firmly with the promoter families, who hold two-thirds of the equity, while named promoters fill four of the seven non-independent board seats (S4, S7).

We could not open the full related-party-transactions section of either the 2025 or the 2026 prospectus. The abridged prospectus does not reproduce it, so we cannot report specific RPT amounts. The related-party features visible in the documents we did read are:

items: Trademark ownership is split. SMC owns 80% of rights in its trademarks after the SAM Global merger, and the remaining 20% is held by promoters Subhash Chand Aggarwal and Mahesh C Gupta personally (S4). Promoters owning part of the brand of a listed company is unusual and creates a potential conflict.

There are many common directorships across group entities. Executives and promoters sit on Moneywise Financial Services, Moneywise Finvest, SMC Insurance Brokers, SMC Global IFSC and Pulin Comtrade/Investments, and independent directors also sit on Moneywise Financial Services and SMC Insurance Brokers (S4).
Group capital is used in a related way: in Sept 2026 SMC and its NBFC subsidiary jointly bought 26.68% of S.K. Offset for about ₹25.9 cr as part of SME IPO market-making (S19).

blocks.text: Assessment: the promoters' 20% trademark interest is a real, if small, governance point. Beyond that, we have no evidence of unusual RPTs, but because the detailed RPT schedule was not read, this is an absence of evidence, not a clean bill of health.

blocks.caption: Outstanding proceedings disclosed in the prospectuses
rows: Company: disciplinary actions by SEBI/exchanges (column as labelled)

blocks.text: Sources: S5, S4. The criminal matters against promoters are mostly complaints by clients or individuals alleging cheating, misappropriation or unauthorised trades, mainly at the investigation stage. They include several 2023 cases in Kolkata and a 2025 Ghaziabad complaint naming the CMD and executive directors (S4). None has resulted in a conviction according to the disclosures, but the count more than doubled in a year (S4, S5). The roughly 2,000 criminal cases filed by subsidiaries are not explained in the abridged document. They may be recovery or cheque-dishonour cases from the NBFC, but that is our inference.

The most serious regulatory event involved subsidiary Pulin Comtrade (formerly SMC Comtrade). In Sept 2023 SEBI cancelled its broker registration over NSEL paired contracts, finding it not 'fit and proper', with money exposure of about ₹2.75 cr (S17). SAT stayed the order (S4). In Sept 2026 the matter was settled under the NSEL Settlement Scheme 2025 for ₹9,10,780 plus a six-month voluntary debarment from proprietary trading and from taking new commodity clients (S18). The prospectus also lists 'inadvertent discrepancies in secretarial filings' and periodic regulatory inspection observations among its top-10 risks (S4).

subsections.title: Credit-relevant risks for an NCD holder

items: 1. Earnings near the rating trigger. FY26 capital-market PBT/NOI was 20.6% against ICRA's 20% negative trigger, and PAT fell to ₹103 cr. Another weak year could bring a downgrade, which would lower the traded value of these NCDs (S6).

2. Regulatory squeeze on the core business. The F&O STT hike (from Apr 2026) and the RBI CMI lending rules (from Jul 2026) hit derivatives broking (~40% of gross broking income) and proprietary trading (₹138 cr in FY26) (S6, S14, S15).

3. Refinancing and liquidity. ₹624 cr of standalone debt is due within six months against ₹152 cr of unused lines and ₹2 cr of free cash, so the company depends on liquidating the MTF book and receivables, the same assets that secure these NCDs (S1, S6).

4. Market and proprietary-trading risk. About 75% of net income is capital-market linked, and ICRA flags 'idiosyncratic risks linked to proprietary trading' and erosion of MTF collateral in a sharp fall (S6).
5. NBFC credit quality. The SME-heavy book with modest borrower profiles had GNPA of 2.99% at Jun-26, and the portfolio shift is unseasoned (S6).

6. Litigation and conduct risk. 16 criminal and 6 regulatory proceedings against the company, 12 criminal complaints against promoters, 70 disciplinary actions listed, and the prospectus flags authorised-person misconduct as a top risk (S4).
7. Secondary-market liquidity. The prospectus warns there may be no active market for the NCDs, so selling before maturity may not be possible at par (S5).

blocks.text: Shared collateral. The security is a pari passu charge, shared with other lenders, over receivables and the MTF book, which are assets whose value moves with the stock market (S1, S2). 110% cover is not a large cushion against a sharp market correction in which both the borrower's earnings and the collateral fall together.

subsections.title: Risks that matter less than they look

blocks.text: Several of the prospectus's top-10 risks are generic to any listed financial firm: dependence on IT systems, competition from mobile apps and interest-rate sensitivity of NCD prices (S4). They are real but do not set SMC apart. The Pulin Comtrade/NSEL overhang, once the most serious governance item, has now been settled for a small sum (S18).

Subsidiary losses are listed as a top risk (S4). The data we could see points to weak, not loss-making, subsidiaries: insurance broking EBIT is low but positive, and the NBFC earned a 1.8% return on managed assets in FY26 (S6, S8). For a lender to the parent, this is a drag on returns rather than a solvency issue.
Equity-market concepts such as listing gains, grey market premium and valuation do not apply to this debt issue and are not part of the case.

Reported management commentary is limited. With the Q1 FY27 results (July 2026), management set out 'strong double-digit profit growth alongside strategic NBFC portfolio adjustment and digital focus'. It cited a 5-year CAGR target of 20%, investment in AI-based digital tools, a shift of broking activity toward cash markets, and a pivot of the NBFC toward secured retail lending with some loan products discontinued (S9). The report does not say whether the 20% target refers to revenue or profit.

items: NBFC: management plans to consolidate AUM over the next 1–2 years through calibrated growth, re-anchoring toward secured micro-LAP and tighter unsecured underwriting (S6).
Insurance broking: upgraded to composite broker (re-insurance) from Aug 2025 (S4). Its revenue grew 44% YoY in Q1 FY27 but margins remain thin (S8).
Capital: a 1:1 bonus issue was approved in Sept 2025 (S4). Debt funding is expected to keep financing exchange margins and MTF growth (S6).
SMC presented at an analyst conference on 29 Sept 2026, but the filing confirms only that no unpublished information would be shared. No new guidance was reported (S20).

blocks.text: Our read: ICRA, not management, gives the most concrete forward view. It expects continued debt-funded growth, an NBFC kept within prudent leverage, and a recovery that is 'contingent on broader capital market activity' (S6). The 20% CAGR aspiration lacks a published bridge and runs into the 2026 STT and RBI headwinds.

subsections.title: What would change the credit view

blocks.text: ICRA's stated triggers are the ones to watch. A sustained fall in capital-market PBT/NOI below 20%, consolidated gearing above 2.5x, or deterioration in NBFC asset quality would be negative. Better scale, market position and sustained profitability would be positive (S6). On current numbers, gearing has room (1.5x) but profitability does not (20.6%) (S6).

The Q1 FY27 numbers (PAT +22% YoY, broking EBIT +18%) are the first test after the April 2026 STT hike (S8). Q2 FY27 is the first quarter under the July 2026 RBI rules (S15), so the H1 FY27 results due in October–November 2026 are the next real data point. They will arrive after this issue closes.
Timing risk for applicants: this issue closes on 16 Oct 2026, before the quarter that shows the first effect of the RBI funding rules is reported.

This report was written on the opening day (5 Oct 2026). We found no category-wise subscription data for the October 2026 issue in any source we could access, so none is reported. Retail NCD issues of this kind allot on a first-come-first-served basis by date of application (S4, S11), so early-day demand matters more than it does for an equity book-build.

blocks.text: Source: S13. The previous issue was carried by retail and non-institutional investors, with no institutional participation. That is typical of A-rated retail NCD issues and means the price check comes from retail demand, not from professional credit investors.
Anchor investors and grey market premium do not apply to a public NCD issue. Subscription levels, high or low, say nothing about the issuer's credit quality and should not drive the decision.

method: The task describes SMCG04 as a mainboard IPO priced at Rs.1000, but SMC Global's equity has been listed on NSE/BSE since 1995. Research established that SMCG04 is the company's October 2026 public issue of secured NCDs with ₹1,000 face value. The report therefore assesses it as a debt investment. The primary October 2026 prospectus was located on SEBI's site (sebi.gov.in attachdocs, Sept 2026), but the PDFs exceeded the fetch tool's 10 MB limit, direct download was not permitted in this environment, and the SEBI filings listing page did not show the SMC entry. As a result, the 2026 series-wise coupons, the exact 2026 objects split, the restated FY26 financials and the full related-party section were NOT read and are flagged as unconfirmed throughout. As substitutes, we read the registrar-hosted abridged prospectuses for the September 2025 and July 2024 NCD issues page by page (financial tables, objects, board, litigation, risk factors). We also read ICRA's 7 Aug 2026 rating rationale in full (FY25/FY26/Q1 FY27 indicators, liquidity, triggers) and cross-checked 2026 issue facts (size, rating, security, dates) across Whalesbook, TipRanks and search-indexed announcements. Several secondary sources describe the issue as '₹750 crore' or '₹1,500 crore'. That is a lakh/crore mis-conversion of ₹7,500 lakh / ₹15,000 lakh, and the correct figures of ₹75 cr base and ₹150 cr maximum are used here. FY26 consolidated revenue and borrowings come from Screener and are not audited prospectus figures. Interest coverage and margin ratios are our own calculations from prospectus figures. S21 was seen only as a search-result headline and was not opened. For S14, S15, S16 and S21 the publication date could not be confirmed, so the access date (2026-10-05) is recorded. No day-1 subscription data was found. Valuation of SMC's listed equity is deliberately excluded.
